History:
64 year old male with history of hypertension, hypothyroidism, reflux disease, and pneumonia in the past who presents now with a one week history of cough and hemoptysis. The patient states that this course of illness is in some way similar to his previous one that resulted in the diagnosis of pneumonia and the subsequent admission. He has not been as short of breath with this illness, but the cough has been much more prominent. The other significant difference with this illness is the presence of coughing up blood. He started very mildly two days ago and this morning at episode of a significant amount of blood in the sputum. It was more than just blood streaking but actually appear to be clots in his opinion. He denied any chest pain although he has noted some discomfort with coughing.
 
Current Medications:
Synthroid 0.1 mg qday
Cardizem CD 240 mg daily
Pepcid 20 mg qhs prn
 
Allergies:
Penicillin - hives
 
Past Medical History:
Pneumonia - admission 7 months ago, no complications
Hypertension
Hypothyroidism
Esophageal Reflux
no history of cardiac disease
 
Social History:
occasional wine and beer on the weekends
quit cigarettes March 1995, 1 pack per day for 35 years
 
Family History:
Father died of an MI, mother died of a stroke
 
Review of Systems:
Constitutional: no weight loss, diet normal, though not eating much lately, walks fairly regularly
Eyes: wears glasses, no change lately, no spots
ENT: cough as above
Resp: as above
CV: no chest pain, palpitations,
GI: no nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, BRBPR
GU: no dysuria or hematuria, awakes once per night to urinate
Neuro: no focal weakness, numbness, or tingling
 
Physical Exam:
Vital Signs: T 99.6, BP 135/88, Pulse 96, RR 22, O2 saturation 93% on room air
General: AOX3, WDWN, no respiratory distress, but coughing frequently
HEENT: Pupils equal and reactive, EOMI, oropharynx markedly erythematous, no exudates
Neck: supple, shotty adenopathy noted
Lungs: clear lung fields, good air movement, frequent coughing, occasional expiratory wheezes
Heart: RRR, no murmurs, gallops, or rubs noted
Abdomen: soft, nontender, NABS, no masses noted
Ext: 2+ pulses, trace edema in the ankles
Neuro: normal gait, normal speech
 
Lab data:
CBC: WBC 11.2, HGB 12.8, HCT 36.2, Platelets 485
Chest X-ray: clear lung fields, questionable hilar adenopathy
 
Treatment:
He was given one albuterol neb treatment which seemed to help his coughing a bit. He was given one dose of IV antibiotics while in our care, Ceftriaxone 1gm IV. He had no evidence of allergic reaction to this.
 
Diagnosis:
Acute Bronchitis with hemoptysis, rule out lung CA
 
Plan:
The patient was discussed with Dr. Schilz, Pulmonology. He recommended antibiotics, bronchodilators, a cough suppressant, a follow up CT scan of the chest to evaluate the mediastinal adenopathy for possible CA, and follow up visit with him. We will begin Ceftin 500 mg BID, albuterol MDI, and Robitussin AC, schedule the CT for this week, and instruct him to follow up with Dr. Schilz as soon as possible following the CT scan.
